dedupe_keys.name: projecting housing effects on heat and cold mortality and energy use in london for typical future years

description: This study by Jonathon Taylor, Phil Symonds, Clare Heaviside, Zaid Chalabi and Michael Davies estimates heat and cold related mortality and space heating energy in London for typical, non-extreme future climates, given projected changes in population and housing, published in Energy and Buildings in 2021 with Wellcome Trust funding through the CUSSH and HEROIC projects. EnergyPlus was used to simulate summer and winter indoor temperatures and heating energy for dwelling archetypes representing the London stock, with characteristics such as floor area, fabric efficiency, wall type, windows, orientation and airtightness taken from the English Housing Survey; a metamodel was applied to a stock dynamically weighted for demolition, new construction and alternative retrofit rates, for a 2005 to 2014 baseline and the 2030s and 2050s, and linked to population projections and exposure-response functions. Coverage: London housing. Access: open access article. Licence: CC BY 4.0. Caveats: typical years, not extreme heatwaves, and results depend on assumed adaptation and occupant behaviour. Simulation uses: an example of linking building stock simulation to health impact assessment for retrofit and overheating policy. Related records: EnergyPlus and the English Housing Survey.

name: Projecting housing effects on heat and cold mortality and energy use in London for typical future years
organisations: UCL Institute for Environmental Design and Engineering
London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine
outcomes: At current retrofit rates about 168 to 174 annual cold deaths per million would typically be avoided by the 2050s (261 to 269 under ambitious retrofit), while heat deaths rise by about 1 per million per year (12 to 13 under ambitious retrofit without adaptation); external shutters could avoid an estimated 38 to 73 per cent of heat deaths in typical future summers.

resources_used: EnergyPlus building physics simulations of London dwelling archetypes (metamodel)
